acakostic11: Nobody asked Teodor Acakostic why he came. Nobody in R-F13 asks that. He was handed a spade before he was handed a rifle.
Teodor Acakostic answered the first call, number 10 on the rolls. Somebody chalked the number on his helmet. It has not washed off yet.
Teodor Acakostic measured the remaining pencil against the remaining paper. For once, the supplies seemed likely to run out together.

At Calvary Farm, Teodor Acakostic of the Hegemony and Yann Vee of the Concord traded insults across the wire for an hour. By the end they were trading recipes. The Concord took Verdel Ridge. Teodor Acakostic watched the officer move a pin on the map and ask for more digging tools.
An unexploded shell lay beside the approach trench. Teodor Acakostic helped steer the carrying party around it and was glad to leave the problem to somebody else.
dick_j0b: The quartermaster asked Arno Dick to sign for the blanket. He examined the blanket and asked whether the holes were included.
femboy_green: The new sniper gave his name as Wendel Green. The corporal looked at his boots, then at the mud, and laughed for the first time in a week.
The first hundred were recognised, and Wendel Green was among them. He wrote the news on the back of an unfinished letter.
Wendel Green held a letter up to the daylight to read the faint last lines. They were only a shopping list, written on reused paper.

Wendel Green noticed a loophole that had been dark for days. He watched it until dusk and wrote down the change. Verdel Ridge is in Concord hands. Wendel Green stopped arguing about the next watch and went to check the stores.
At the Sunken Road, Wendel Green of the Hegemony and Oskar Eddie of the Concord spent the morning shooting at the same loose sheet of metal. The sheet kept winning.
reza_zdsh: Nobody saw Silas Zdsh arrive. One morning there was simply one more helmet in S-F10, and a quiet field cook under it.
The colonel shook hands with the first hundred, one by one. Silas Zdsh was number 21. He still remembers how cold the colonel's glove was.
Silas Zdsh tried to write neatly for the first line of a letter. By the third, he was writing as quickly as the thoughts arrived.
Yann Vee (Concord) and Silas Zdsh (Hegemony) met in the same shell hole at Calvary Farm during a raid. They stared at each other. Then each crawled home, and neither has told anyone.
Edmund Matteozrybak wrote a letter for Silas Zdsh's mother, because Silas could not find the words. Silas signed it.
Edmund Acquillae taught Silas Zdsh to play the harmonica. The bay has asked them both, formally, to stop.

Marek Red (Concord) and Silas Zdsh (Hegemony) spotted the same abandoned cart near Calvary Farm. A long exchange of shots left the cart exactly where it was. From Verdel Ridge the Concord guns have a clear view. Silas Zdsh wrote to his mother, who writes every Sunday that night and said only: 'We will take it back.'
The salvo walked along S-F10 and caught Silas Zdsh in the open. Two men carried him back between salvos. A bed came free in the hospital dugout, and Silas Zdsh was carried in at last.
